title: Your life as an Imperial Assassin(Warhammer 40k)
fullText: You're 12 when they execute your parents in the street. Public hanging. Official charges say treason against the Imperia. The actual crime was reporting the local governor for embezzling taxes meant for the Imperial Guard. The governor had connections. Your parents had principles. Principles lose every time. You watch from the crowd because they make everyone watch. That's the whole point. Compliance through terror. The Imperium's favorite teaching method since like forever. Your father's last words are something about the emperor protecting the faithful. Your mother only mouthed, "Live." The governor watches from his balcony, satisfied. Two weeks later, that same governor is found dead in his private chambers. Throat cut. No witnesses, no suspects. Clean, professional work. The arbitrators call it a mystery. The new governor, who actually distributes taxes correctly, calls it divine intervention. You know better. God doesn't work like that. After all, your parents were very much dead. So, you learn a different truth. The world needs justice. And what the Imperium needs for that are executioners. You spend 3 years looking for the people who understand that. Or more accurately, for them to let you find them, hard to tell which. A woman sits down across from you in a transit station one day. Doesn't introduce herself. Just starts talking like you're already made conversation. The official assassin. You've been asking questions in the right places. They have answers. She explains what it costs. 90% of recruits die in training. The survivors stop being people and become weapons instead. No family, no attachments, no future except whatever mission they assign you. You ask where to sign. She almost smiles. Terra, she says, tomorrow bring nothing. The facility is deep underground, the kind of place that doesn't exist on any official maps. You arrive with 43 other orphans. All of you angry about something. All of you wanting the same thing. Nobody's ready for what comes next. First 3 months are physical conditioning. They break your body down completely. Then rebuild it with augmentations and gene therapy. Your skeleton gets reinforced. Reflexes get enhanced beyond human limits. 90% of candidates die during this phase. Hearts give out under the strain. Neural systems reject the implants. bodies just fail completely. [screaming] You survive. Month four, they start education. Imperial history, xenos biology, chaos, corruption, political structures. Basically teaching you how the Imperium actually functions versus how it claims to function. Month six, they show you why precision matters. Two planets on the display. Both have the same problem. Genesteeler cult infestation. Planet one, single Kadus assassin. 6 months of infiltration, 47 precise kills. Cult leadership eliminated. Network collapses completely. 3 billion civilians saved. Planet 2. Inquisitor calls Exterminatus. Vir responds to the entire world. 8 billion dead. The math is right there. One surgical death prevents genocide. Overkill just is genocide. You get it. Month seven, they pair you with another recruit girl named Kessa. You train together for weeks, cover each other's mistakes, start trusting each other. Then they hand you a blade and tell you to kill her. She's standing across the room. Both of you knew this was always the end point. You complete the test. Months 8 through 12 are psychological conditioning. Neural implants go in. Cybernetic threads woven through your brain that suppress emotions during operations. You can feel things after the mission if you want, never during. Anger becomes threat assessment. Fear becomes risk calculation. Personal attachment gets flagged as tactical liability and deleted. You stop having feelings and start having mission parameters instead. Year two brings specialization assignments. There is six temples, six different methods. Vindicare are snipers. Aversur are drug field berserkers. Collelex are anti-csycer blanks. Vanis handle information warfare. Venom are poison specialists. Kaladus are infiltrators. Deception skills, adaptability, capacity for identity suppression. You test high for Kaladus aptitude. The Kaladus temple takes you. Grandmaster Draon Vangoric visits your temple twice during advanced training. He's one of the 12 high lords of terror, master of the official assassinorum. Not what you expect from a high lord. No theatrics, no grand speeches, just competent and practical, focused on results. He watches you run infiltration exercises, takes notes, doesn't say much. After your fifth successful mission, he calls you in personally. corrupt planetary governor embezzlement case 16 officials funneling guard tides into personal accounts. You eliminated the ring leader and the entire network collapsed within a week. Vanor reviews the report in front of you. Points out that most high lords need six committees and a year of debate to make basic decisions. Meanwhile, soldiers are dying because some bureaucrat delayed their equipment shipments. The Imperium needs precision, he explains. Needs people who can bypass the paralysis and actually fix problems. Makes complete sense. He seems like the only high lord who actually cares about making the system work instead of just maintaining his position. Everyone thinks so. And while our protagonist takes orders from a high lord, today's sponsor puts you in charge of your own war effort. Warhammer 40,000 Tacticus. So, Tacticus is a turnbased tactical strategy where you build a roster of 120 plus champions across 22 factions and throw them into fast hex grid skirmishes. And what faction you pick actually changes how you play. different abilities, different positioning, different ways of winning a fight, so you end up building around a faction and learning how it works. Also, the matches are short, so you can knock a few out before bed. Right now, Tacticus is celebrating its 4-year anniversary with a two-eek long event, so exclusive content, daily missions, the usual celebration stuff, and the major new event, the epic crusade mode. Crusade is a full galactic war across about 96 planets. Imperials push their crusade. Chaos and the Xenos factions push back and every guild picks a side. Whoever holds the most planets when the season ends wins. It's the mode I'm looking forward to the most because it means my guild and I are grinding toward the same planet instead of doing our own separate things. Season 1 kicks off August 9th and it unlocks a power level 20. Three new champions dropped this month, too. Starting with Ramis, the veteran sergeant of the Dark Angels, followed by Scitar, robot of the Thousand Sons, and finally, Darnath Lzander of the Imperial Fists on August 30th, who buffs Terminators and teleports them into the fight. Download Tacticas free with my link below, or scan the QR code on screen now, and use code game for Crusade for 2,000 gold, one requisition order, and five shards of Trejan. Valid until September 15th. All right, back to the official assassin. 17 years later, new assignment. Lord Commander Militin Veritus Kain, one of the 12 High Lords of Terror, commands all Imperial Guard forces across the galaxy. Also completely incompetent, delays deployments for politics, get soldiers killed through bureaucratic stubbornness. Your assignment, infiltrate the Imperial Palace, map his patterns, execute when ordered. Timeline: 6 months of preparation. Cover identity. Palace administrative clerk. Records department. Boring. Forgettable. Polymorphine injection. Polymorphine lets you reshape your body completely. Become anyone. Kill from the inside. The mirror shows a middle-ag bureaucrat with bad posture. Perfect. Standard work. Routine surveillance. Mapping Kane's schedule. Guard rotations. Vulnerability windows. Week three. Arbitrators show up for a random audit. They pull files, ask questions about transfer histories, look for documentation gaps, standard intimidation tactics. Your cover is perfect, so you're fine. Don't panic. Don't scramble. Don't call anyone. Lyra is working across the hall and notices. Lyra Castellan, adept of the administrative. The title means she investigates. Whatever the administrative decides needs investigating, which right now is high-ranking personnel disappearing from palace departments. She's minor nobility, the kind with enough status for juvenile treatments, but not enough wealth to avoid actually working. In her case, that means tracking 14 people who've vanished in the last 3 months. Her problem, she needs access to Lord Commander Kane's classified personnel files, but his entire department is compromised. Everyone in that office reports to him. Everyone covers for each other except you. You've only been there 3 weeks. Haven't been around long enough to be part of whatever is happening. She approaches you in the records archive. Makes her pitch directly. She needs someone with access to Kane systems who isn't already compromised. Smart approach. She's asking you to betray your department head, which happens to be exactly your actual assignment. So, you agree. She gets her investigation access. You get deeper into Kane security patterns. Tactical cooperation. She's mapping the disappearances, pulls up her full analysis, shows you the pattern. 14 people gone. All connected to different high lords. Not just Cain. All 12. Same timing windows. Same methodology. You look at the data and your blood runs cold. You were briefed on Kain. One target, one assassination. This is 12 simultaneous operations. That's official methodology. All of it. Someone's targeting the entire senatorum. She says, "You already know who because you're part of it. Just didn't know how big it was." She keeps digging. You keep helping, knowing exactly what she's going to find. Late night, still reviewing files together. She mentions she doesn't sleep well. Sees faces, people she's lost. Small admission, didn't mean to share it. You don't file it away as useful intelligence. Don't analyze it tactically. You just listen. She notices, sees something in your reaction. You've lost someone, too. Not a question, a statement. You don't answer. Can't. But you don't deny it either. First crack in the armor. Month two. Late night in the records department. She shows you the photo. Her sister Ara organized food distribution in the lower hives. Fed thousands of people who would have starved. Official killed her 8 years ago, preventing radical elements. One death prevents millions. That's what they believe, right? They killed the person, preventing millions from starving. She's not angry, just tired, grieving still. Your philosophy says one surgical death prevents genocide. Her reality says they murdered someone actively saving lives. I know they think they're saving the Imperium. Maybe they are, but they don't see who they're killing to do it. First time, the math doesn't add up. You think she's right. You think she's also wrong. You think this is more complicated than training suggested. The conditioning should flag this attachment compromise. Mission liability. It doesn't activate or maybe you ignore it. Hard to tell which. Month four. She asks about your past, where you're from, your family, why you never talk about yourself. Standard deflection would be easy. Boring bureaucrat backstory. Maintain the cover. Instead, you pause. Almost tell her something real about your parents, about the execution, about why you became this. The words are right there. You stop yourself. Nothing worth talking about, you say. But she saw it. That split second where you almost let her in. Someday, she says quietly. When this is over, you can tell me. You know you never will. Doesn't stop you from wishing you could. Month six. You still haven't received the order to execute Kane, but you've already mapped out the perfect plan. Even a rookie Kaledus could kill him now. Lyra is discussing her next plan with you. Just before she mentions the witness, she says something that lands wrong. I trust you. You know that, right? You should feel nothing. Mission asset expressing confidence and cover identity. Instead, it hits like a blade between the ribs. She chose to trust you despite any doubts, despite your secrets. That makes what you're about to do so much worse. She finds a witness, palace administrator, who saw something, terrified, hiding in the underhive levels. She needs help extracting him safely, asks you. You agree because of course you do. The extraction is simple enough. Small records room three floors down. No surveillance coverage. Elias steps out to check the corridor. Make sure the exit route is clear. You're alone with the witness. Maybe 30 seconds. He's nervous. Keeps talking, describing what he saw. synchronized timing, final preparations, coordinated strikes across all 12 High Lord residences. He's describing the beheading in enough detail that if [snorts] he testifies, the entire operation gets exposed prematurely. Your protocols run the calculation automatically. Threat level, compromise, potential, mission priority. The opportunity is perfect. No witnesses except one. Quick solution. Clean and professional. Neck snap. You're checking his pulse to confirm when you hear it. The door opening. She's standing there. She sees you standing over the body, hands still on his neck. Perfect assassin kill positioning. Her face goes through several expressions very fast. Confusion, realization, horror, pure dumb luck. She came back exactly when she did. She's smart enough to know a professional kill when she sees one. She's armed before you can say anything. Small pistol from inside her coat, pointed directly at you. Hands shaking slightly, but aim steady enough. What did you do? No good answer to that question. Who are you? Also no good answer. Long silence. You standing over a body. Her pointing a gun. Both of you knowing everything just changed completely. She backs toward the door. Weapon never wavering. Stay away from me. She doesn't finish the threat. Just leaves. You don't follow. You report the compromise immediately. Witness eliminated but cover burned. The response comes back. Extraction protocols activate. Maintain position. You try to find her. She's gone. Beheading proceeds in 48 hours. They pull you back to the shrouds. Cover compromise. New assignment. 48 hours later. It happens. 11 assassins, 11 targets, 11 strikes. All the other high lords die within 1 hour. Fangoric orchestrated the whole thing. He's one of the 12, the Grand Master of Assassins. He survives, obviously, and stalls puppet replacements for the dead ones, people he controls. For the good of the Imperium, he says, temporary measures until stability returns. 100 years later, stability still hasn't returned. Turns out temporary is Imperial code for indefinitely tyrannical. Venoric's rule gets worse every decade. More paranoid, more brutal, more assassinations of anyone who questions him. You spend a century doing what you were trained for, eliminating his enemies, maintaining his control. Standard work. Very precise. Very wrong. Then Lord Commander Maximus Thne decides enough is enough. Thain, chapter master of the Imperial Fists, war hero decorated across 50 campaigns. the kind of officer who actually believes the Emperor's ideals means something beyond propaganda. He's been watching Vangor's tyranny for decades. Tried negotiations, tried reforms, tried working through proper Imperial channels. Nothing worked. The tyrant just got worse. So makes a simple decision. Voric dies. He gathers three Space Marine chapters, 400 Aardis, the Emperor's finest warriors, Imperial Fists, Sable Swords, Halo Brethren. They breach the assassin or temple on Teride Dawn. VanGor deploys everything. 100 Eversaur assassins, drugfueled Berserkers. The temple becomes absolute slaughter. You're inside when it starts, initially just surviving. Then you see what's happening. Eversource tearing through space murders. Vanoric's final madness. This isn't precision. This is extinction. Fighting through carnage when you hear something. Turn around. Lyra face to face. 5 m. Both wounded. Both covered in blood. Just staring. Everything unsaid. The betrayal. The work. 100 years ago. What you felt. What she felt. All right. There. Neither speaks. Then you see it over her shoulder. Vindicare elevated, lining up a shot. Could warn her, could take the shot. You never miss, but conditioning kicks hard. She's investigating corruption. Knows what you are. Liability. Eliminate the compromise. You freeze. Can't choose. Split second lasting forever. Her people rush in, dragging her to cover. She disappears. You try following. Can't lose track of them completely. On the other side, Thane fights through hell to reach Vangoric and kills him, ending the battle. 100 Eversaurs dead, 399 Space Marines dead. That's it. So, the Imperium restructured everything after that. New high llords appointed, new rules implemented. The Inquisition created the Ordo Sicarius. Permanent oversight of all assassins, assassin Inquisitors embedded in every temple of spies. One attempted dictatorship and 200 deaths later, the Imperium invents workplace oversight. Progress, new requirements, no deployment without twothirds vote from the Highlords. Detailed mission reports, regular psychoindoctrination sessions. They disperse the temples, scattered them across the galaxy. One falls to corruption. The others remain untainted. The scalpel got a leash. Finally, you survived the restructuring. Listed as recovered, reassigned. The psycho indoctrination came monthly. Inquisitor watching, analyzing, looking for compromise, for attachment, for weakness. You passed everyone. Neural conditioning still functional. Mostly functional. Functional enough. They never asked about the woman in the corridor. Never asked you why you hesitated. Some glitches don't show up in scans. Two years later, different city, different face, different life. New assignment, market surveillance, midday crowd, tracking a corrupt official. Standard work. This is what you are. This is what you do. The crowd thickens. People passing in all directions. Then a figure passes close. She turns away, disappears into the crowd. You continue your surveillance. [music] The Imperium protects [music]
fullTextVi: Bạn 12 tuổi khi họ xử tử cha mẹ bạn trên đường phố. Treo cổ công khai. Các cáo buộc chính thức nói rằng đó là tội phản quốc chống lại Imperia. Tội ác thực sự là tố cáo thống đốc địa phương về tội tham ô thuế dành cho Vệ binh Hoàng gia. Thống đốc có mối quan hệ. Cha mẹ bạn có nguyên tắc. Nguyên tắc lần nào cũng thua. Bạn xem từ đám đông vì họ khiến mọi người phải xem. Đó là toàn bộ vấn đề. Tuân thủ thông qua khủng bố. Phương pháp giảng dạy được yêu thích nhất của Imperium kể từ đó mãi mãi. Những lời cuối cùng của cha bạn là về việc hoàng đế bảo vệ những người trung thành. Mẹ bạn chỉ nói: "Trực tiếp. " Thống đốc nhìn từ ban công, hài lòng. Hai tuần sau, người ta phát hiện vị thống đốc đó đã chết trong phòng riêng của ông ta. Cắt cổ họng. Không có nhân chứng, không có nghi phạm. Làm việc sạch sẽ, chuyên nghiệp. Các trọng tài gọi đó là một bí ẩn. Thống đốc mới, người thực sự phân phối thuế một cách chính xác, gọi đó là sự can thiệp thần thánh. Bạn biết rõ hơn. Chúa không làm việc như vậy. Suy cho cùng, bố mẹ bạn đã chết rất nhiều. Vì vậy, bạn học được một sự thật khác. Thế giới cần sự công bằng. Và thứ mà Imperium cần cho việc đó là những kẻ hành quyết. Bạn dành 3 năm để tìm kiếm những người hiểu được điều đó. Hay chính xác hơn là để họ cho phép bạn tìm thấy họ, khó có thể nói đó là gì. Một ngày nọ, một người phụ nữ ngồi đối diện bạn ở một trạm trung chuyển. Không giới thiệu bản thân. Chỉ cần bắt đầu nói chuyện như thể bạn đã bắt đầu cuộc trò chuyện. Sát thủ chính thức. Bạn đã đặt câu hỏi ở đúng nơi. Họ có câu trả lời. Cô ấy giải thích chi phí của nó. 90% tân binh chết trong quá trình huấn luyện. Những người sống sót không còn là con người nữa mà trở thành vũ khí. Không gia đình, không ràng buộc, không tương lai ngoại trừ nhiệm vụ họ giao cho bạn. Bạn hỏi nơi để ký. Cô gần như mỉm cười. Terra, cô ấy nói, ngày mai chẳng mang theo gì cả. Cơ sở này nằm sâu dưới lòng đất, một nơi không hề tồn tại trên bất kỳ nào bản đồ chính thức. Bạn đến cùng với 43 đứa trẻ mồ côi khác. Tất cả các bạn đều tức giận về điều gì đó. Tất cả các bạn đều mong muốn điều tương tự. Không ai sẵn sàng cho những gì tiếp theo. 3 tháng đầu là thời gian rèn luyện thể chất. Chúng phá hủy hoàn toàn cơ thể bạn. Sau đó xây dựng lại nó bằng các phương pháp tăng cường và liệu pháp gen. Bộ xương của bạn được củng cố. Phản xạ được tăng cường vượt quá giới hạn của con người. 90% ứng viên chết trong giai đoạn này. Trái tim dâng lên dưới sự căng thẳng. Hệ thống thần kinh từ chối cấy ghép. cơ thể chỉ thất bại hoàn toàn. [la hét] Bạn sống sót. Tháng thứ tư, họ bắt đầu đi học. Lịch sử đế quốc, sinh học xenos, hỗn loạn, tham nhũng, cơ cấu chính trị. Về cơ bản dạy cho bạn cách Imperium thực sự hoạt động so với cách nó tuyên bố hoạt động. Tháng thứ sáu, chúng cho bạn thấy tại sao độ chính xác lại quan trọng. Hai hành tinh trên màn hình. Cả hai đều có cùng một vấn đề. Sự phá hoại của giáo phái Genesteeler. Hành tinh một, sát thủ Kadus độc thân. 6 tháng xâm nhập, 47 lần tiêu diệt chính xác. Lãnh đạo giáo phái bị loại bỏ. Mạng sụp đổ hoàn toàn. 3 tỷ thường dân được cứu. Hành tinh 2. Người điều tra gọi Exterminatus. Vir đáp lại toàn bộ thế giới. 8 tỷ người chết. Toán học ở ngay đó. Một cái chết phẫu thuật ngăn chặn nạn diệt chủng. Quá mức cần thiết chỉ là diệt chủng. Bạn hiểu rồi. Tháng thứ bảy, họ ghép bạn với một cô gái tuyển dụng khác tên là Kessa. Bạn tập luyện cùng nhau trong nhiều tuần, che đậy lỗi lầm của nhau, bắt đầu tin tưởng lẫn nhau. Sau đó, họ đưa cho bạn một con dao và bảo bạn giết cô ấy. Cô ấy đang đứng bên kia phòng. Cả hai bạn đều biết đây luôn là điểm kết thúc. Bạn hoàn thành bài kiểm tra. Tháng 8 đến tháng 12 là giai đoạn điều hòa tâm lý. Cấy ghép thần kinh đi vào. Các sợi từ tính dệt xuyên qua não bạn để ngăn chặn cảm xúc trong quá trình hoạt động. Bạn có thể cảm nhận mọi thứ sau nhiệm vụ nếu bạn muốn, không bao giờ trong suốt nhiệm vụ. Sự tức giận trở thành đánh giá mối đe dọa. Nỗi sợ hãi trở thành sự tính toán rủi ro. Tệp đính kèm cá nhân được gắn cờ là trách nhiệm pháp lý và bị xóa. Bạn ngừng có cảm xúc và thay vào đó bắt đầu có các thông số nhiệm vụ. Năm thứ hai mang đến các bài tập chuyên môn. Có sáu ngôi chùa, sáu phương pháp khác nhau. Vindicare là tay bắn tỉa. Aversur là những kẻ điên cuồng trong lĩnh vực ma túy. Collelex là khoảng trống chống csycer. Vanis xử lý chiến tranh thông tin. Nọc độc là chuyên gia về chất độc. Kaladus là những kẻ xâm nhập. Kỹ năng lừa dối, khả năng thích ứng, khả năng đàn áp danh tính. Bạn kiểm tra năng khiếu của Kaladus rất cao. Ngôi đền Kaladus sẽ đưa bạn đến. Grandmaster Draon Vangoric đến thăm ngôi đền của bạn hai lần trong quá trình đào tạo nâng cao. Anh ta là một trong 12 chúa tể khủng bố, chủ nhân của nhóm sát thủ chính thức. Không phải những gì bạn mong đợi từ một lãnh chúa cấp cao. Không sân khấu, không có bài phát biểu hoành tráng, chỉ có năng lực và thực tế, tập trung vào kết quả. Anh ấy nhìn bạn thực hiện các bài tập xâm nhập, ghi chép, không nói nhiều. Sau nhiệm vụ thành công thứ năm của bạn, anh ấy sẽ đích thân gọi bạn đến. vụ án tham ô thống đốc hành tinh tham ô 16 quan chức chuyển tiền bảo vệ vào tài khoản cá nhân. Bạn đã loại bỏ kẻ cầm đầu và toàn bộ mạng lưới sụp đổ trong vòng một tuần. Vanor xem lại báo cáo trước mặt bạn. Chỉ ra rằng hầu hết các lãnh chúa cấp cao đều cần sáu ủy ban và một năm tranh luận để đưa ra những quyết định cơ bản. Trong khi đó, binh lính đang chết vì một số quan chức đã trì hoãn việc vận chuyển thiết bị của họ. Ông giải thích rằng Imperium cần sự chính xác. Cần những người có thể vượt qua tình trạng tê liệt và thực sự khắc phục được vấn đề. Hoàn toàn có ý nghĩa. Anh ta có vẻ như là lãnh chúa tối cao duy nhất thực sự quan tâm đến việc tạo ra hệ thống làm việc thay vì chỉ duy trì vị trí của mình. Mọi người đều nghĩ vậy. segments.text: He survives, obviously, and stalls puppet replacements for the dead ones, people he controls.
segments.viText: Rõ ràng là anh ta sống sót và ngăn chặn việc thay thế con rối cho những người đã chết, những người mà anh ta điều khiển.

segments.text: For the good of the Imperium, he says, temporary measures until stability returns.
segments.viText: Ông nói, vì lợi ích của Đế quốc, các biện pháp tạm thời cho đến khi ổn định trở lại.

segments.text: 100 years later, stability still hasn't returned.
segments.viText: 100 năm sau, sự ổn định vẫn chưa trở lại.

segments.text: Turns out temporary is Imperial code for indefinitely tyrannical.
segments.viText: Hóa ra tạm thời là mã của Đế quốc chuyên chế vô thời hạn.

segments.text: Venoric's rule gets worse every decade.
segments.viText: Sự cai trị của Venoric trở nên tồi tệ hơn sau mỗi thập kỷ.

segments.text: More paranoid, more brutal, more assassinations of anyone who questions him.
segments.viText: Hoang tưởng hơn, tàn bạo hơn, ám sát nhiều hơn bất cứ ai tra hỏi anh ta.

segments.text: So, the Imperium restructured everything after that.

segments.text: Progress, new requirements, no deployment without twothirds vote from the Highlords.
